outcome: No result advancing, refuting, or otherwise changing the bound in Hall's conjecture (either the classical form |y^2 - x^3| > c(epsilon) x^{1/2-epsilon}, or the original conjectured form) was found in the 26 January 2024 - 22 September 2026 window.
summary: Hall's conjecture concerns the separation between perfect squares and perfect cubes on Mordell curves y^2 = x^3 + k, and its weak form (with the epsilon and constant c(epsilon), as stated in the frozen Wikipedia bullet) remains open. All pre-2024 history is well documented: Elkies' 1998 discovery of a case (x=5853886516781223, from a curve with |k| large) that disproved the strong (epsilon=0) form, forcing the weaker epsilon-dependent version now standard; Danilov's 1982 proof that exponent 1/2 is essentially optimal; and an extensive, continually updated table of 'Hall numbers' (record small ratios r_x) maintained by Dujella and collaborators, most entries from the 1990s-2000s with a 2014 paper (Karim & Silverman, arXiv:1410.0078) on gap sizes between consecutive Hall numbers, none after 2024. Multiple targeted searches (general web search and arXiv search across 2024-2026) turned up no preprint, announcement, or new record-table entry addressing this problem in the window. General AI-and-mathematics search terms (AlphaEvolve, AlphaProof, DeepMind Erdos-problem sweeps, GPT-based Erdos-problem solutions) surfaced substantial 2025-2026 AI activity on other open number-theory and combinatorics problems (e.g., the unit distance conjecture, various Erdos problems), but none of that coverage mentions Hall's conjecture, Mordell curves, or the square-cube gap problem. Per the scope rule (3.1), record-table extensions (new Hall numbers) would only count if found, since the bullet is about the existence/value of a bound rather than being itself a 'largest known value' bullet — but no such extensions were found in any case. I agree with the triage's verdict: nothing has happened to this problem in the window, and no AI system is connected to it.
competing_reading: None identified. There is no ambiguous or borderline result to classify differently; the search simply returned nothing in-window. If an unindexed table update (e.g., an informal addition to Dujella's personal 'Hall numbers' webpage, which I could not access directly - it returned 404) occurred without an accompanying paper, it would not surface in these searches, but such an update would at most be 'progress' on the record table, not a change to the stated bound itself under the scope rule.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement post-26-January-2024 either (a) proving or disproving the weak form of Hall's conjecture, (b) improving the known exponent/lower-bound results (e.g., beating Danilov's or subsequent bounds), or (c) adding entries to the Hall-number record table with a dated publication. None of these were found.
